subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: The Texas City Refinery Explosion
description: A quick win: understand The Texas City Refinery Explosion.

hook.text: On March 23, 2005, an explosion at BP's Texas City refinery killed 15 workers and injured 180 others.

buildup.text: A distillation tower was being restarted. Operators overfilled it with flammable hydrocarbon liquid beyond safe levels.

discovery.text: The blowdown drum — designed to safely vent excess liquid — overflowed. A geyser of hydrocarbons ignited near a running truck.

twist.text: BP had cut the refinery's maintenance budget by 25%. Workers used temporary office trailers parked dangerously close to the unit.

climax.text: The Chemical Safety Board's investigation led to sweeping refinery safety reforms and new process safety management standards.

punchline.text: Budget cuts. Trailers too close. A restart gone wrong.

quiz.question: What immediate cause triggered the Texas City refinery explosion?
options: A corroded pipeline burst and sprayed fuel onto a hot surface
An overfilled tower vented hydrocarbons that ignited near a running vehicle
An electrical fault in the control room sparked in a gas-filled area
